requirements.original: The hexadecimal digits represent the numeric code point of the character.
requirements.canonical: The hexadecimal digits of a short identifier ARE representing the numeric code point of the character.

examples.text: (e.g. char(U0171) denotes the Latin small letter u with double acute: "ű").

requirements.original: In the USI-like notation, the leading zeroes can be omitted, (i.e. char(U171)is equal to char(U0171)).
requirements.canonical: Leading zeroes of a short identifier in the USI-like notation MAY be omitted (char(U171) is equal to char(U0171)).
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.1.0 -- In the USI-like notation, the leading zeroes can be omitted, (i.e. char(U171)is equal to char(U0171)).

requirements.original: NOTE 5: Control characters can be denoted by using the predefined conversion function, the quadruple form or the USI-like notation.
requirements.canonical: A control character CAN be denoted in a `universal charstring` value by the predefined conversion function, the quadruple form or the USI-like notation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.1.0 -- NOTE 5: Control characters can be denoted by using the predefined conversion function, the quadruple form or the USI-like notation.

requirements.original: By default, universal charstring shall conform to the UTF-32 encoding specified in clause 9.3 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2].
requirements.canonical: By default, a `universal charstring` SHALL conform to the UTF-32 encoding specified in clause 9.3 of ISO/IEC 10646.

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether this constrains the internal value representation or the default encoding applied by encoding functions; the encoding reading was chosen as the observable one.
readings: By default, the encoding of a `universal charstring` value (e.g. by encoding functions) SHALL be UTF-32.
By default, the internal representation of a `universal charstring` value SHALL be UTF-32.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.1.0 -- By default, universal charstring shall conform to the UTF-32 encoding specified in clause 9.3 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2].

requirements.original: This default encoding can be overridden using the defined variant attributes (see clause 27.5).
requirements.canonical: The default UTF-32 encoding of a `universal charstring` MAY be overridden using the defined variant attributes.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.1.1.0 -- This default encoding can be overridden using the defined variant attributes (see clause 27.5).
